newsitem.title: USA: SEC seeks proposals for second-generation EDGAR.
newsitem.headline: SEC seeks proposals for second-generation EDGAR.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday it has started soliciting offers for the construction and operation of a second-generation electronic filing system.
The effort is aimed at modernizing SEC's EDGAR, short for Electronic Data Gathering and Retrieval, which Congress wants to be privatized.
EDGAR started as a pilot project eight years ago and began receiving filings from publicly held corporations in 1993. It now accepts filings from up to 15,000 companies.

The filings include initial public offerings, registration statements for equity and debt offerings, disclosures of share acquisitions, tender offers, quarterly and annual financial statements and other reports.
The SEC said all offers are due at its headquarters here no later than 3 p.m. EST on January 24. It said it will hold a conference with possible bidders at 2 p.m. on November 21.
The agency said it would consult with Congress and the Office of Management and Budget before awarding any contract.

Congress, under a securities regulatory reform law enacted earlier this year, called for the SEC to examine proposals to privatize EDGAR and to make a report within six months on how it would contract out work on the successor to the system.
Currently, much of the work on EDGAR is contracted to BDM International Inc Inc, a Virginia-based technology company.
The SEC has spent about $80 million to fund EDGAR, said David Copenhafer, an agency official who oversees the project.
